step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-Stage CMOS Operational Amplifier with Cascode Bias
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.8 shows the complete schematic of the two-stage CMOS op-amp consisting of an NMOS differential pair (M1, M2) with PMOS active load mirror (M3, M4), cascode tail current source (M6T, M6B), and a PMOS common-source second stage (M7) loaded by an NMOS cascode current sink (M8T, M8B). The DC transfer curves and input offset characteristics are shown in Figures 24.3 and 24.4 on pages 775 and 776.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent DC power dissipation of the op-amp core

equation.explanation: Sum of constant currents supplied to the differential stage and output stage multiplied by supply voltage VDD.
equation.assumptions: M6 tail current is 20 uA, M8 second-stage pull-down is 10 uA; VDD = 1.8 V.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = (20uA + 10uA) * 1.8V = 30uA * 1.8V = 54 uW (excluding bias generator). If including SUB_1 bias network (~30-50 uA total), P_total ≈ 100-150 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: In SKY130 with VDD=1.8V and nominal branch currents around 10-20 uA, core static power is ~54 uW.

maximum_output_voltage.description: Maximum output voltage swing (V_OH) limited by M7 saturation

source.reference: Section 'Output Swing and Current Sourcing/Sinking Capability'

equation.explanation: The maximum output voltage is limited by PMOS output transistor M7 entering the triode region.
equation.assumptions: V_DSsat7 ≈ 100 mV to 150 mV across M7.

sky130_expected.reasoning: M7 requires at least V_ov ≈ 100-150 mV to remain in saturation.

minimum_output_voltage.description: Minimum output voltage swing (V_OL) limited by M8 cascode saturation

source.reference: Section 'Output Swing and Current Sourcing/Sinking Capability'

equation.explanation: The minimum output voltage is set when cascode current sink transistors M8T/M8B remain in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Two stacked saturated NMOS devices require roughly 200-250 mV total headroom.

equation.explanation: Mismatch between stage 1 quiescent output voltage and stage 2 M7 gate-source requirement creates a systematic shift in the DC transfer curve.
equation.assumptions: Properly sized mirror ratio M7/M4 = 2*(I_M8/I_M6) yields near 0 offset; deliberate sizing mismatch shifts V_OS.

sky130_expected.calculation: For balanced design: V_OS ≈ 0 mV. For slight systematic mismatch: |V_OS| < 5 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Systematic offset depends on the W/L ratio matching between M4/M7 and current branch balance.

dc_open_loop_gain.description: Low frequency open-loop voltage gain A_OL,DC

equation.explanation: Product of the first-stage gain (g_m1 * (r_on || r_op)) and second-stage gain (g_m2 * (r_op || R_ocasn)).

sky130_expected.calculation: In SKY130: g_m1 = sqrt(2*un*Cox*(W/L)*Id) ≈ sqrt(2*270u*10*10u) = 232 uA/V. r_o ≈ 1/(lambda*Id) = 1/(0.1*10u) = 1 MΩ. R_1 ≈ 500 kΩ -> Stage 1 gain ≈ 116. Stage 2 cascode load R_2 ≈ 1 MΩ, g_m2 ≈ 200 uA/V -> Stage 2 gain ≈ 200. Total gain ≈ 23200 ≈ 87 dB without heavy loading; with realistic channel length modulation and substrate effects, 60 to 75 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Two gain stages in 130nm CMOS provide between 55 dB and 75 dB of DC voltage gain.

first_pole_frequency.description: Dominant pole frequency f_1 created at high impedance node 1 via Miller effect

equation.explanation: Miller multiplied capacitance C_c at node 1 along with stage resistance sets the dominant low-frequency pole.
equation.assumptions: R_1 ≈ 111 kΩ, R_2 ≈ 333 kΩ, g_m2 = 150 uA/V, C_c = 100 fF gives f_1 ≈ 287 kHz.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depending on C_c (100 fF - 2.4 pF as discussed in text), f_1 falls between 3 kHz and 300 kHz.

equation.explanation: The frequency where the extrapolated or actual open-loop gain drops to 0 dB.
equation.assumptions: Single-pole rolloff governed by input transconductance g_m1 and compensation capacitance C_c.

sky130_expected.calculation: For g_m1 ≈ 200 uA/V and C_c = 2.4 pF: f_un = 200u / (2*pi * 2.4p) ≈ 13.3 MHz. For C_c = 1 pF: f_un ≈ 31.8 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 transconductance is slightly higher than 150 uA/V, yielding ~10-25 MHz for Cc ≈ 1-2 pF.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the open-loop op-amp at unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Stability measure indicating the phase distance from -180° when loop gain magnitude is unity.
equation.assumptions: Unity feedback (beta = 1) is the worst-case stability condition.

sky130_expected.calculation: Without adequate C_c (e.g. C_c=100fF), op-amp is unstable (PM < 0°). With C_c ≈ 2.4 pF and zero-nulling resistor R_z, target PM is 60° to 80°.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Stable closed-loop operation requires PM >= 60 degrees.

source.reference: Section 'Output Swing and Current Sourcing/Sinking Capability'

equation.explanation: The maximum sinking current is limited by the constant current sink M8.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The cascode current sink M8T/M8B pulls a constant 10 uA.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive SPICE testbench for the two-stage op-amp measuring DC power dissipation, DC transfer curve, systematic offset, output swing limits, open-loop frequency response (A_OL, f_un, PM) using Baker's AC open-loop simulation configuration (Fig. 24.9) and DC sweep (Fig. 24.4a).
